# `Browser.Microphone`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Microphone — capture a bounded audio clip from the device
microphone as a base-64 `data:` URL, over `Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism: an outbound `JsCmd`
carries the recording options; the host starts `getUserMedia({ audio: true })`,
arms a `MediaRecorder`, buffers the chunk stream, stops after `maxDurationMs`
milliseconds, assembles the chunks into a single Blob, reads it via
`FileReader.readAsDataURL`, and pushes ONE inbound `JsMsg` carrying the
assembled clip. Both directions cross the same seal codec and fail-closed port
discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

This is the ONE-SHOT microphone member of the `Ipe.Browser` device family,
exactly as `Ipe.Browser.Geolocation.current` is the one-shot member of
geolocation. Audio STREAMING (chunks as they arrive) is a separate, session-
level primitive and is NOT part of this module.

The `maxDurationMs` option is capped at 8 000 ms (8 seconds) on the JS side.
This ceiling keeps the full round-trip well within the `Js.request` per-waiter
deadline of 10 seconds (blob assembly and the `FileReader` read happen after
the recording stops, so a 10 s deadline requires a ≤ 8 s recording). A caller
that supplies a larger value silently records for 8 s. If you need a longer
clip, batch multiple `captureAudio` calls.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses `js-port:microphone`
(import-derived, keyed on the canonical `Ipe.Browser.Microphone` path prefix via
`WebCapability::for_browser_module`, alias-immune); only the top-level app's
`[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.Microphone.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound ADTs
    and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` wiring.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `captureAudio` returns a
    `Task Error AudioClip` via the correlated port→Task bridge; a host permission
    denial or an absent `MediaRecorder` resolves to a typed `Err`. The inbound
    `case` is EXHAUSTIVE: every variant becomes either an `Ok` or a typed `Err`,
    never a silently dropped frame or a panic.

## `Options`

Recording options. `maxDurationMs` is the maximum recording length in
milliseconds (capped at 8 000 by the JS sink); `mimeType` is the preferred
MIME type passed to `MediaRecorder` (e.g. `"audio/webm"`) — the browser may
fall back to its own default if the type is unsupported, and the actual MIME
type used is returned in `AudioClip.mime`.

## `AudioClip`

A captured audio clip: the assembled audio data encoded as a `data:` URL
(e.g. `data:audio/webm;base64,...`), the MIME type the browser actually used,
and the actual recording duration in milliseconds (clamped to `maxDurationMs`).

## `captureAudio`

```ipe
captureAudio : Options -> Task Error AudioClip
```

`captureAudio opts` — record an audio clip for at most `opts.maxDurationMs`
milliseconds, as a `Task Error AudioClip`.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). The served JS handler
calls `getUserMedia({ audio: true })`, starts a `MediaRecorder`, collects
`ondataavailable` chunks, stops after `maxDurationMs` milliseconds (capped at
8 000 ms — see module note), assembles the chunks into one Blob, reads it via
`FileReader.readAsDataURL`, and resolves the `Task` with the result. A host
permission denial (`NotAllowedError`) resolves to `Err permissionDenied`; an
absent `getUserMedia` or `MediaRecorder` resolves to `Err unavailable`.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:microphone`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort Microphone ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `recordings`

```ipe
recordings : (Result Error AudioClip -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`recordings toMsg` — the inbound subscription, wired in `subscriptions`.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into a
`Result Error AudioClip`.
